controls.title: Validate privileged-access requests
controls.statement: Validate and authorise the business need for privileged access before activating it. Limit the granted permissions to the approved duties.
controls.risk: Administrator access granted without a valid need could allow unauthorised changes, disclosure of sensitive information or disruption of services.
controls.scope: Requests for new or changed privileged access to systems and data.
controls.examine: Sample new requests, approvals, business justifications and actual permissions. Compare validation and approval timestamps with account activation.
controls.interview: Ask the approving owner how business need is established, who can approve access and how exceptions are handled.
controls.test: Trace sampled requests through the workflow. Confirm that granted permissions match the approved duties and that activation followed validation.
test_steps: Select a risk-based sample of approved, rejected, emergency and expired privileged-access requests from different systems and requestors.
For each sample, compare the requested role and duration with the named duties, system owner approval, requester identity validation and any segregation-of-duties check.
Compare the approved scope and activation window with the permissions actually granted and the platform audit trail; record any access granted early, beyond scope or without all approvals.
For rejected and expired requests, verify through an effective-permissions query or safe access attempt that no privileged capability remains.
controls.expected: Each sampled grant has a validated need, an authorised decision and permissions matching that decision before activation.

mappings.basis: Validating initial requests is the central requirement.
Validates the initial permission set; ongoing least privilege also requires access review.
Covers privileged access; the safeguard also covers other enterprise access and role changes.
Supports approval and provisioning requirements, not every account lifecycle activity.
This is an anti-pattern: access is provisioned before need is confirmed. Use it to identify a failure condition, not as a required practice.

controls.title: Separate administrative accounts
controls.statement: Assign dedicated administrator accounts for privileged work. Use non-privileged accounts for routine email, browsing and office work.
controls.risk: Using administrator accounts for everyday work could allow a malicious email or website to cause widespread damage.
controls.scope: Human users who perform administrative duties.
controls.examine: Compare personnel, account inventories and assigned roles. Inspect separation between routine and administrative identities.
controls.interview: Ask administrators how they switch accounts and how emergency access is managed.
controls.test: Sample administrators and verify that routine accounts cannot perform privileged actions. Review whether dedicated accounts are being used for routine activities.
test_steps: Select administrators from infrastructure, applications, cloud services and security tools, including at least one recently appointed or transferred administrator.
Inspect each person's ordinary and administrative accounts, group memberships and sign-in history; confirm the privileged identity is distinct and attributable to one person.
Using authorised test accounts, attempt one privileged action with the ordinary account and one routine activity such as email or web browsing with the administrative account.
Confirm the ordinary action is denied, the privileged action succeeds only through the dedicated account, and both outcomes are recorded with the correct identity.
controls.expected: Administrative identities are separate and used only for duties requiring privilege; routine identities lack unnecessary administrative rights.

mappings.basis: Requires a dedicated privileged account used solely for privileged duties.
Separates administrator accounts from general computing activities.
Account separation helps limit privileged credentials to the processes that require them; it does not alone enforce all use restrictions.
Supports restriction of privileged accounts; the source also requires the organisation to define the allowed personnel or roles.

controls.title: Require strong authentication for administrative access
controls.statement: Require multi-factor authentication for human administrative access. Identify entry points and prevent alternative sign-in paths from bypassing it.
controls.risk: A stolen administrator password could give an attacker control of important systems if no additional identity check is required.
controls.scope: Human administrative accounts, remote access paths and supported applications, including externally managed services.
controls.examine: Compare privileged accounts and administrative entry points with authentication policies, exclusions and sign-in records.
controls.interview: Ask the identity owner how new services, recovery paths and emergency accounts are covered.
controls.test: Use an authorised test account to verify the additional factor and check alternative sign-in routes for bypasses.
test_steps: Choose representative administrative paths, including local, remote, console, command-line, recovery and emergency access where they exist.
Sign in with an authorised privileged test account through each path and verify the required independent authentication factors and approved device or network conditions.
Attempt safe bypass cases such as a legacy protocol, alternate interface, expired session, factor removal or account-recovery route.
Verify bypass attempts fail or follow an approved exception, and trace successful and failed events to central monitoring with the user, path, time and factor result.
controls.expected: In-scope administrative sign-ins require the prescribed factors; unsupported systems and exceptions are identified and reviewed against the applicable source requirements.

mappings.basis: Requires multi-factor authentication for privileged human users.
Retain the safeguard’s where-supported condition and third-party scope.
Requires multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts.
Covers privileged human access; the source also covers other high-risk access and permits other credential approaches.

controls.title: Review and remove unnecessary privileged access
controls.statement: Review privileged access at an agreed frequency and when roles or responsibilities change. Remove or adjust access that is no longer needed.
controls.risk: Unnecessary administrator access could be misused after a person changes roles or leaves, putting information and services at risk.
controls.scope: Privileged identities, permissions, temporary grants and account owners.
controls.examine: Compare current access with personnel changes, review decisions and removal records. Identify temporary, dormant and ownerless accounts.
controls.interview: Ask reviewers how they validate continuing need and ensure decisions are carried out.
controls.test: Sample retained and removed access. Verify business need, review dates and completed permission changes against the applicable deadlines.
test_steps: Recreate the review population from live privileged groups, roles, local administrators, cloud entitlements and emergency accounts rather than relying only on the review export.
Sample retained, reduced and removed access and compare each decision with current duties, owner approval, last use, conflicts and the required review date.
Query effective permissions after the review to verify approved reductions and removals reached every relevant system and inherited access path.
Calculate completion times for departures, transfers and high-risk findings and record overdue access, unsupported retention or review populations that omitted live privileges.
controls.expected: Reviews and triggered changes are completed on time; each retained privilege is justified and removal decisions are implemented. Source-specific deadlines must be checked separately.

mappings.basis: Specifically requires disabling privileged access after 12 months unless revalidated; verify this deadline.
Requires disabling privileged access after 45 days of inactivity; scheduled reviews alone do not satisfy this condition.
Covers privileged reviews; the safeguard also requires role definitions and reviews at least annually across enterprise assets.
Review privileges and reassign or remove them; the organisation must define the frequency and covered roles.
Includes periodic reviews and triggers such as organisational changes and temporary elevation.
Anti-pattern describing failure to validate continuing need during reviews.

controls.title: Record privileged activity
controls.statement: Record privileged access and administrative actions in central logs that identify the actor, time, target and action. Protect those records against unauthorised changes.
controls.risk: Without reliable records of administrator activity, harmful changes could go unnoticed and an investigation may not establish what happened.
controls.scope: Privileged sign-ins and administrative actions on in-scope systems, including third-party administration.
controls.examine: Compare the system inventory with collected log sources. Inspect event fields, central collection and protection settings.
controls.interview: Ask the logging owner how missing sources, collection failures and access to records are managed.
controls.test: Perform an authorised benign administrative action and trace its record to central storage. Verify actor, time, target and action, and test protection using test records.
test_steps: Perform authorised benign administrative actions through interactive, command-line and automated privileged paths on representative systems.
Trace each action from the source system into central storage and confirm the record contains the individual actor, privileged identity, time source, target, action and outcome.
Using a non-authorised account, attempt to alter or delete a test record and change logging configuration; confirm prevention or immediate detection and alerting.
Retrieve the test events using normal investigation tools and from the oldest required retention period to confirm records remain searchable, readable and attributable.
controls.expected: Sampled activity is recorded centrally with sufficient detail to trace it, and unauthorised changes to records are prevented.

mappings.basis: Specifically requires central logging of privileged access events.
Covers protection from changes; also verify the source requirement to prevent unauthorised access, including reading.
Requires logging the execution of privileged functions.
Covers privileged events; the safeguard requires audit logging more broadly across enterprise assets.
Anti-pattern describing third-party privileged access that is not logged.
